correctness.rationale: The cited exceptional-index criterion counts n in the argument b(2n), not n in b(n). Its dyadic strata have densities 2^(-2k-4) and bounded counting error per stratum. For u_n=(-1)^tau(n), pairing the even and odd starting positions gives C(2M)=-M-C(M) and C(2M+1)=C(2M)-1, so C(N)+N/3=O(log(N+2)); the bounded one-point sums then give the four ordered pair rates. The only possibly nonempty positions in block 16n+[0,15] are 0,2,8,10, with indicators chi(n),tau(n),1_{n even}tau(n),1-tau(n). An exceptional block index has even parity of digit sum, is even, and has a nonexceptional predecessor of even digit-sum parity. These facts give the eight transitions in (5), with no missing transitions. Internal and boundary gaps then give rates per 16-block 1/3,1/3,1/12,1/4,1/4,1/12 in the stated order. A cutoff through a partial block costs O(1), and substituting the cutoff at f_J uses f_J=12J+O(log(J+2)) and counts exactly the first J starting points. An independent coin-change calculation using the three-square obstruction corroborated all six counts at four irregular cutoffs; it is not the proof of the error bound.
residual_risks: Uses the cited exact exceptional-index characterization; does not settle automaticity of the ordered gap sequence.
